reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding is effective for surface modification and that HEAs have desirable properties, but it does not provide specific prior evidence for the key premises regarding HEA cladding on tool steels, its dual-phase microstructure, or its superiority over fusion welding in mitigating hot cracking and improving hot corrosion.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a metallurgically bonded, low-dilution coating on steels.
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) can provide high corrosion resistance and excellent mechanical properties.
Laser cladding of HEAs can produce a refined, dual-phase (FCC/BCC) microstructure.
The HEA coating will mitigate hot cracking compared to traditional fusion welding repair.
The HEA coating will improve surface hardness, wear resistance, and hot corrosion performance.
